After leaving Facebook, the user was surprised that no open source tool recreated its stacking workflow. They call Graphite "a god send in my post FB career."
Ex-FAANG engineer says stacking was a meaningful time-saver for them as a software engineer.
"I've tired the CLI, but couldn't get into it. I'll have to try the VSCode extension and give it another shot."

Has used Graphite for a few months and is really enjoying it ("finally works on cygwin!"). The command name change will take getting used to. Hit a 1.0 bug where it queries git for an object (something with ^tree) it doesn't understand, possibly a git version issue.
Asks for a setting to auto-delete branches after merging on app.graphite.dev. Without manually deleting branches after a merge, `repo sync`/`sync` doesn't detect that a branch has been merged.

Used it for months, "an absolute joy to use." Annoyance: their org enforces signed commits, and merging a stack sometimes rebases commits internally and loses the signing. That causes an error when merging the rest of the stack.
Misses stacked diffs from working at FB. Says Graphite looks like the best way to be productive outside FAANG internal tooling.
"Graphite and stacked diffs are awesome!" The user misses Phabricator from their time at Uber and had been sad that nobody built a superior developer experience on the same concepts.
Has followed Graphite for a while but wishes it supported GitLab. Their employer uses GitLab, so they can't adopt it.
Has used it for more than a year and it is part of their toolbelt. They especially value the CLI's ability to seamlessly rebase multiple branches at once. "Powerful tool, and nice community."

Compared to other stacking tools (e.g. git branchless), the main improvement is that Graphite keeps all stacking metadata in git refs. With the other tools they couldn't figure out how to develop a stack across multiple machines.
"Graphite is incredible and has absolutely improved my team's velocity. Highly recommend!"
"I'm really used to my Graphite workflow and I can't imagine going without it anymore." The user worries the Cursor acquisition is normally not good news for the product.

Graphite's core stacked-PRs feature is "really good despite all the AI things they've added around their review UI." After the Cursor acquisition, the user doubts their team will keep relying on it for long.
"Graphite was basically what GitHub should have been but never was."
"Graphite is a fantastic tool that I use every day." By contrast, the user no longer sees much use case for Cursor and questions whether joining Cursor was the best exit for Graphite.
Earlier called it a shame where Graphite was headed with AI and sees the acquisition as "the final nail in the original product's coffin." Recommends git spice and jujutsu as replacements.
Reacting to the acquisition news: "Well, time to bite the bullet and learn jujutsu over the holidays."
